item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State House of Assembly, on Tuesday, threw its weight behind the creation of state police, passing the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, with all 22 members present voting in favour and none against, as lawmakers pushed for a decentralised policing system to tackle insecurity. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent from plenary during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in the country. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to supporting constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. He stressed that implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, argued that policing must be brought closer to the people. He said a decentralised system would sharpen security responses and address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies, to ensure the proposed State Police Services complement existing security structures and improve overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, insisted on adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect the fundamental rights of citizens. Lawmakers also cited improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as key benefits of a decentralised policing system. The passage marks the Assembly’s formal endorsement of the proposed amendments, paving the way for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. item.description: Ebola virus is a dangerous virus that causes Ebola virus disease (EVD), a serious infectious illness that can be fatal. The virus can spread from infected animals to humans and from one infected person to another through direct contact with infected blood and other bodily fluids. Ebola can cause fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. In severe cases, the disease can damage vital organs and cause bleeding. However, not everyone who contracts Ebola dies. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. Humans may become infected through contact with infected wild animals, including fruit bats, monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and other susceptible animals. Symptoms usually appear between two and 21 days after exposure to the virus, although they often begin within eight to 10 days. Early symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, extreme weakness, tiredness, muscle and joint pain, sore throat and loss of appetite. item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO: Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he plans to defect from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the claims as false and misleading. The former Sokoto State governor, through his media office, said he had no intention of leaving the ADC, warning that the speculation could create unnecessary confusion ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement dated October 19, 2026, and signed by Prince Daniel, Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to the senator, Tambuwal’s media office reaffirmed his commitment to the ADC and its political objectives. “For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Tambuwal has no plans to join the APC. Suggestions to the contrary are false, baseless and should be disregarded,” the statement said. The clarification comes amid heightened political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 elections, as parties and their leading figures position themselves for the contest. However, the media office insisted that the reports should not be interpreted as an indication of any impending change in Tambuwal’s party affiliation. item.title: Governance will suffer if Tinubu campaigns nationwide — Ex-Obidient Chief
item.description: …Challenges critics to debate fuel subsidy removal By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Director-General of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance, also known as the Tinubu Must Stay (TMS) Movement, Marcel Ngogbehei, has said governance could suffer if President Bola Tinubu personally campaigns across all 36 states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient Movement, also challenged critics of the removal of the petrol subsidy to an open debate on the policy, urging them to offer alternatives that take Nigeria’s economic realities into account. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja alongside the National Coordinator of the movement, Engr. Ibrahim Said Uba, during a media parley where he explained why the President might not personally attend campaign activities in every state. “One of the greatest challenges we are having in this country is the time to govern and the time to do electioneering,” Ngogbehei said. He argued that the early commencement of political mobilisation for subsequent elections had undermined governance, with political actors shifting attention away from delivering on their mandates. “A president gets into office, and one year after he gets into office, they start preparing for the next election. And what suffers? Governance suffers,” he said. According to him, Tinubu has chosen to delegate campaign responsibilities to trusted associates to enable him to concentrate on governance. “The President has said, ‘I want to focus on governance. I want to keep an eye on the key things that I am doing. Let the people I have worked with go out there and do the work.’ And in some instances where I need to come in, I will come in. item.content:encoded: …Challenges critics to debate fuel subsidy removal By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Director-General of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance, also known as the Tinubu Must Stay (TMS) Movement, Marcel Ngogbehei, has said governance could suffer if President Bola Tinubu personally campaigns across all 36 states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient Movement, also challenged critics of the removal of the petrol subsidy to an open debate on the policy, urging them to offer alternatives that take Nigeria’s economic realities into account. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja alongside the National Coordinator of the movement, Engr. Ibrahim Said Uba, during a media parley where he explained why the President might not personally attend campaign activities in every state. “One of the greatest challenges we are having in this country is the time to govern and the time to do electioneering,” Ngogbehei said. He argued that the early commencement of political mobilisation for subsequent elections had undermined governance, with political actors shifting attention away from delivering on their mandates. “A president gets into office, and one year after he gets into office, they start preparing for the next election. And what suffers? Governance suffers,” he said. According to him, Tinubu has chosen to delegate campaign responsibilities to trusted associates to enable him to concentrate on governance. “The President has said, ‘I want to focus on governance. I want to keep an eye on the key things that I am doing. Let the people I have worked with go out there and do the work.’ And in some instances where I need to come in, I will come in. It is pure delegation,” he said. Ngogbehei maintained that effective leadership required building strong teams and institutions rather than depending solely on the physical presence of the leader. “Every good leader must not always be there. If you are a leader that has built resources, that built people, you should trust your people to do the job,” he said. He added: “We don’t want to have a country where you have strong personalities and weak institutions. And that is what we are trying to build for Nigeria.” The TMS director-general urged Nigerians to consider the implications of requiring the President to attend campaign events in every state, arguing that the time devoted to electioneering could come at the expense of governance. “Imagine that the President says, ‘Okay, I am going to be in all the campaigns in thirty-six states of the country.’ What suffers? That is the bottom line. “He can go round the country if he wants to go round, and he has been going round. But let us just understand with him in this particular instance,” he said. Challenges critics to subsidy debate On the removal of the petrol subsidy, Ngogbehei invited critics of the policy to a public discussion on the rationale behind the decision and the alternatives available to the government. He said participants should examine the challenges the policy was intended to address and assess whether alternative approaches could deliver better outcomes. “We are telling the person, let us sit down and let us x-ray these things. “You need to first of all show us that you understand the problem and then, if you were there, what would you do differently, putting into consideration all the complexities of Nigeria?” he asked. Ngogbehei said the invitation was open to individuals and groups, regardless of their political affiliations. “We are open to have this discussion with anyone, anytime, any day. Let us just be open, let us be transparent, let us be factual. It is our country. We cannot run it by propaganda. We cannot run it by lies,” he said. Borrowing would have worsened situation — Uba In his remarks, Uba warned that continued borrowing to sustain the subsidy regime could have exposed the country to more severe fiscal difficulties. item.title: Abiodun mourns Fasoranti, describes him as democratic icon
item.description: Gov. Dapo Abiodun of Ogun has expressed sorrow over the death of elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing it as a monumental loss to Nigeria. In a statement on Tuesday in Abeokuta, Abiodun, Chairman of the Southern Governors’ Forum, conveyed his condolences to Afenifere, Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo, Yoruba leaders, and the deceased’s family and associates. The governor described Fasoranti, who recently celebrated his 100th birthday, as a patriot whose life was defined by service and commitment to the advancement of the Yoruba nation and Nigeria. He said the late elder statesman was among the enduring voices in Nigeria’s democratic struggle, whose courage and sacrifices helped shape the country’s political development. Abiodun noted that Fasoranti played a significant role in the struggle for democracy, particularly during military rule, earning recognition as a defender of democratic governance and constitutional rule. He said the deceased remained steadfast in advocating justice, equity, good governance and restructuring, demonstrating his commitment to building a united and prosperous Nigeria. The governor described Fasoranti as one of the surviving links to a generation of nationalist leaders who confronted authoritarianism and championed democratic freedoms. “The elder statesman’s death has created a significant vacuum in the Yoruba socio-political landscape; his contributions to national development remains indelible. “Fasoranti’s legacy will endure through the values he upheld, the causes he championed, and the generations of Nigerians inspired by his commitment to democracy,” he said. He urged Afenifere, the people of Ondo, the Yoruba nation and the deceased’s family to take solace in his remarkable life and contributions to society. item.title: Why I rejected Real Madrid, Inter Milan, Bayern Munich — Gerrard
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard has revealed why he turned down interest from European giants Real Madrid, Inter Milan and Bayern Munich, insisting he has no regrets about remaining at Anfield during his playing career. As reported by ESPN, Gerrard disclosed his decision while speaking on the Overlap Daily podcast, explaining that he was never keen on leaving Liverpool despite interest from some of Europe’s biggest clubs. “I had some interest from foreign teams and the majority of that was through [now Real Madrid coach] José Mourinho,” Gerrard said. “Inter Milan, Real Madrid, on a couple of occasions, and at the back end a few conversations with my agent when [Bastian] Schweinsteiger was leaving Bayern [in 2015].” The former England captain said he was content at Liverpool, particularly during Brendan Rodgers’ time as manager, and had little interest in pursuing a move abroad. “I wasn’t really that interested in it because I was never going to leave Liverpool at the time. I was enjoying my football under [coach] Brendan [Rodgers] when that one came but yes, three or four of the big teams showed some interest during my career, which is flattering, of course it is,” he added. Gerrard, who made 710 appearances for Liverpool and won nine trophies during his 19-year playing career, admitted that watching English players such as Jude Bellingham at Real Madrid and Harry Kane at Bayern Munich enjoy success abroad sometimes makes him reflect on what might have happened had he left Anfield. “When you watch the likes of Jude Bellingham [at Real Madrid] and Harry Kane [at Bayern Munich] and you see them winning loads of trophies with foreign teams, it does cross your mind and you go back and you think,” he said. “But I have no regrets in terms of the decisions I made. No regrets.” Gerrard retired from international football in 2014 and ended his playing career in 2016 after a spell with Major League Soccer side LA Galaxy, having joined the American club in 2015. He subsequently moved into management, taking charge of Rangers and Aston Villa before managing Saudi Pro League side Al Ettifaq. He has been without a club since leaving the Saudi Arabian side in January 2025. item.title: Reps probe SGF’s approval for lawmakers’ foreign trips
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has mandated its Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate a circular requiring the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) to approve official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. The House also reaffirmed the constitutional independence of the legislature, warning that subjecting lawmakers’ official foreign travel to executive approval could undermine the principle of separation of powers. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi, who drew the House’s attention to a circular dated August 13, 2026, with reference number PRS59648/5.13/TI/335, issued by the Office of the SGF. The circular reportedly requires prior approval from the SGF before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs can issue Notes Verbales for official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. Moving the motion, Onuakalusi expressed concern that the requirement could compromise legislative independence, impede parliamentary diplomacy and create an inappropriate system of executive control over the legislature. He maintained that the National Assembly was an independent arm of government, not a ministry, department, agency or subordinate institution of the executive. The lawmaker cited Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which establish the legislature, executive and judiciary as distinct arms of government founded on the principles of separation of powers and checks and balances. He also referenced Section 51 of the Constitution and Section 22 of the National Assembly Act, 2014, in reaffirming the legislature’s constitutional status and authority over its internal administrative arrangements. Onuakalusi stressed that executive administrative procedures must respect constitutional boundaries and should not interfere with the legislature’s ability to discharge its constitutional responsibilities. Following the adoption of the motion, the House directed the Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate the circular and its implications for parliamentary independence. The committees are expected to recommend appropriate legislative action and report back to the House within four weeks for further consideration. The resolution reinforces the House’s position that administrative procedures introduced by the executive must not undermine the autonomy of the National Assembly or interfere with its constitutional functions. The association called on lawmakers to introduce safeguards against unilateral regulatory decisions, strengthen coordination among existing institutions and amend the Bill to prevent duplication, regulatory uncertainty and unnecessary disruption to businesses. It stressed that a coherent regulatory environment was essential for investment, economic growth, effective public-health protection and compliance with the law. The association said effective regulation should be based on clearly defined institutional responsibilities, predictable compliance requirements, proportionate enforcement and coordination among relevant government agencies. It expressed readiness to engage further with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to achieve a legislative outcome that protects public health while sustaining regulatory certainty and business confidence. Health Ministry, SON seek deferment The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare also expressed reservations about the proposed amendments at a public hearing on the Bill. Represented by Dr Adebisi Adegoke, mni, Director of Hospital Services, the Ministry raised concerns about potential regulatory conflicts, duplication and overlapping mandates, which it said could undermine effective government administration. It recommended deferring consideration of the Bill to allow further consultations among affected stakeholders and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s existing responsibilities. SON similarly raised concerns that some provisions of the proposed legislation conflicted with the law establishing the organisation and could interfere with its statutory responsibilities. The standards body backed the call for the Bill’s consideration to be deferred, arguing that a more comprehensive review was needed to remove unnecessary complexities and overlapping mandates. It also expressed concern that the process leading to the proposed amendments had not involved sufficient engagement and consultation with affected institutions. Industry operators warn of business disruption Tobacco industry operators have also expressed reservations about the proposed legislation, warning that another layer of regulation could complicate compliance rather than improve regulatory effectiveness. At a recent public hearing, industry stakeholders argued that tobacco manufacturing, importation, distribution, packaging, health warnings, product standards and related activities were already subject to extensive statutory controls. They warned that parallel approval and enforcement structures could expose manufacturers and importers to conflicting directives, additional administrative costs, operational disruptions and uncertainty over which regulator has final authority. The operators maintained that their concerns were not about resisting public-health regulation but about the risks of multiplying regulatory requirements without clearly demonstrated public-policy benefits. item.title: Uduaghan’s remains arrive in Warri, as Oborevwori visits family
item.description: Obi, Ebie, Obaseki, Iyovwaye pay tributes to former Delta governor By Jimitota Onoyume WARRI — The remains of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, arrived in the state on Tuesday, as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and his wife, Deaconess Tobore Oborevwori, joined members of the deceased’s family to receive them at Osubi Airport in Okpe Local Government Area. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, for consideration and approval. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services alongside the Federal Police Service as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. Presenting the committee’s report, its chairman and member representing Qua’an-Pan South Constituency, Theodore Maiyaki, said the proposed amendment was necessary in view of prevailing security challenges, manpower shortages in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen policing at the grassroots. He explained that the proposal would establish a framework for federal and state policing, with safeguards for human rights, operational standards, accountability and coordination. The committee also noted that improved security was critical to the socioeconomic development of Plateau State and the country at large, recommending that the House support the proposed constitutional alteration. Following deliberations, lawmakers adopted the recommendations and voted in support of the proposed amendment. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, commended the committee for its work and thanked members for their patience, commitment and sacrifice in considering the legislative proposal. The constitutional amendment requires approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly before it can proceed to the next stage of the process. Meanwhile, the House passed two other bills for first reading: the Plateau State Right of Patients and Medical Institutions Bill and the Plateau State Bill on Jungle Justice, Mob Action and Other Forms of Unlawful Violence Against Persons. The bills will undergo further legislative consideration in line with the rules of the Assembly. The House subsequently resolved to proceed on recess from Monday, October 19, to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, to allow members to rest and prepare for upcoming legislative responsibilities. The Speaker appreciated lawmakers, supporting staff, and other personnel for their dedication to the service of Plateau State, noting that the Assembly had continued its legislative duties beyond the initially scheduled recess period.
